title: Class Blueprint, Constructor __init__, and Multiple Instances
code:
# Defining the Class Blueprint
class Student:
    def __init__(self, name, age, mark):
        # Binding instance attributes via self
        self.name = name
        self.age = age
        self.mark = mark

    def display(self):
        print(f"Scholar: {self.name:<8} | Age: {self.age} | Mark: {self.mark}")

# Creating multiple independent objects from the same blueprint
s1 = Student("Arun", 20, 85)
s2 = Student("Priya", 19, 92)
s3 = Student("Rahul", 21, 75)

print("===== COHORT ROSTER =====")
s1.display()
s2.display()
s3.display()

# Modifying s1 has zero effect on s2 or s3
s1.mark = 88
print(f"Updated {s1.name}'s mark to: {s1.mark} (Priya is still {s2.mark})")
explanation: Demonstrates the relationship between a class blueprint, __init__ constructor, self reference, and creating independent instances with isolated memory state.

title: Encapsulated State: BankAccount with Transaction Methods
code:
class BankAccount:
    def __init__(self, holder, initial_balance=0):
        if initial_balance < 0:
            raise ValueError("Initial balance cannot be negative")
        self.holder = holder
        self.balance = initial_balance

    def deposit(self, amount):
        if amount <= 0:
            print("Deposit amount must be positive")
            return False
        self.balance += amount
        return True

    def withdraw(self, amount):
        if amount > self.balance:
            print(f"Insufficient balance! Attempted: ${amount}, Available: ${self.balance}")
            return False
        self.balance -= amount
        return True

    def display(self):
        print(f"Account Holder: {self.holder} | Current Balance: ${self.balance}")

# Transaction Workflow
account = BankAccount("Arun", 5000)
account.deposit(1000)
account.withdraw(2500)
account.display()

# Attempting overdraft
account.withdraw(9000)
account.display()
explanation: Shows how methods encapsulate business logic, protecting the object's internal state (balance) from invalid mutations and overdrafts.
